relations.subject: Eugen Julius Theodor Hultzsch
relations.evidence: Hultzsch studied at the Dresden College of the Sacred Cross and the University of Lipsia, where he studied Oriental languages.

relations.subject: Eugen Julius Theodor Hultzsch
relations.role: Chief Epigraphist to the Government of Madras
relations.evidence: In 1886, Hultzsch moved to and settled down in India, where he was employed by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) as Chief Epigraphist to the Government of Madras.

relations.subject: Eugen Julius Theodor Hultzsch
relations.evidence: In 1903, Hultzsch resigned from the ASI and returned to Europe, where he served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Halle.

relations.subject: Valaiyattur Venkayya
relations.evidence: Hultzsch was succeeded as Chief Epigraphist by Valaiyattur Venkayya.
